about.anything_you_add_stays_on: Anything you add stays on this device: your library is stored locally in this browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
about.every_cabinet_represents_somebody_: Every cabinet reflects a lot of careful work: photographing artwork, mapping lamps, measuring reels, dumping ROMs and preserving documentation.
about.for_testing_fruitulator_on_far: Thanks to everyone who tested Fruitulator on more machines than its authors could reach themselves, and sent feedback along the way.
about.free_software_under_the_gnu: Free software under the GNU AGPL 3.0 licence.
about.fruitulator_lets_you_play_classic: Fruitulator lets you play classic fruit machines on any device with a modern web browser.
about.it_runs_the_original_game: It runs the original game ROMs on emulated hardware and displays them using layouts created by the fruit-machine community.
about.john_recovered_the_fml_layout: Paul wrote the `.fml` layout decoder, and John built Oasis around it. Oasis's layout decoder and system-specific game configuration maps have also been invaluable references for Fruitulator's layout and `.gam` handling. Much of what appears on screen here is possible because of that work.
about.mame_has_been_an_important: MAME has been an important reference throughout Fruitulator's development, particularly for understanding the hardware used by different fruit-machine platforms and the behaviour of devices such as steppers, displays, sound hardware and characterisers.
about.particular_thanks_to_james_wallace: Particular thanks to James Wallace and David Haywood for their work on fruit-machine hardware, and to the many MAME contributors whose research and device implementations have helped document these systems.
about.report_a_bug_or_suggest: Report a bug or suggest a feature
about.the_68000_cpu_core_is: The 68000 CPU core is tested instruction by instruction against the SingleStepTests vectors.
about.the_layout_authors_rom_dumpers: The layout authors, ROM dumpers and manual scanners
about.the_ym2413_implementation_is_based: The YM2413 implementation is based on emu2413 and has been checked against it for accurate output. Its instrument tables also draw on research by andete and die analysis by Nuke.YKT.

arcade.guide.export_games: To share the games in your arcade, select **Export games** on your arcade card. This creates a single `.punnet` file. Anyone who imports it into their library can play those machines in your arcade.
arcade.guide.host_one: You can host one arcade of your own. Share its link to invite others, or set it to **Public** to make it appear in the arcade list.
arcade.guide.in_beta: The arcade is in beta, so your arcade setups and balances may be lost during future updates.
arcade.guide.no_personal_details: There’s no email address or password. The arcade never asks for your real name or other personal details. Other players can only see the player name you choose and, if you add one, your profile picture.
arcade.guide.one_player: Only one person can play a machine at a time. Any credits left on a machine stay there for the next player, so be sure to collect them before leaving.
arcade.guide.own_library_only: You can only play machines that are in your own library. In someone else’s arcade, any machine that hasn’t been imported into your library will be unavailable to play.
arcade.guide.passkey: You need to log in to build an arcade or play in one. Sign in with a passkey using your phone, computer or security key, authenticated with your fingerprint, face or PIN.
arcade.guide.payday: Payday is every night at midnight UTC. If your balance is below £10, it’s topped up to £10.
arcade.guide.play_money: It’s play money only - you can’t buy more or cash it out.
arcade.guide.starting_wallet: Everyone starts with £20 in a shared wallet that can be used in any arcade.

arcade.privacy.each_machine_keeps_its_ow: Each machine keeps its own record of who's playing (using a random account number, not your name), which buttons they press, saved games, and money taken and paid out. This lets people share a machine fairly and keeps the totals accurate.
arcade.privacy.how_the_arcade_keeps_your: How the arcade keeps your details
arcade.privacy.if_you_host_an_arcade: If you host an arcade, anyone who opens its link can see its name, room, picture and game names. These details also appear in the arcade list if you make it Public.
arcade.privacy.if_you_log_in_another: If you log in another device with a code, the arcade keeps the name of that device's browser and system (such as "Firefox on Linux") for 10 minutes at most, so you can check it is yours. It goes once that device is logged in.
arcade.privacy.no_adverts_no_tracking_or: No adverts, tracking, analytics or third-party logins. Nothing is sold or shared.
arcade.privacy.questions_about_your_deta: Questions about your details, or a request to see or remove them, by email:
arcade.privacy.tap_your_player_icon_at: Tap your player icon in the top-right corner and choose Delete my account. This deletes your player name, picture, passkeys, logins on all devices, wallet and wallet history, visits and stars. Any arcade you host will also be taken down.
arcade.privacy.the_arcade_runs_on_cloudf: The arcade runs on Cloudflare. As with any website, your IP address and browser details pass through Cloudflare with each request. Cloudflare keeps the arcade's request logs for up to 7 days, and a backup history of its records for up to 30 days. The arcade does not keep your IP address in its own records.
arcade.privacy.the_arcade_uses_two_cooki: The arcade uses two cookies. One remembers for 24 hours that you've confirmed you're 18 or over. The other keeps you logged in (see below). Both are needed for the arcade to work, so there's no cookie banner.
arcade.privacy.the_arcades_you_have_visi: The arcades you have visited (the first and last time) and the stars you give them.
arcade.privacy.the_login_cookie_it_keeps: The login cookie. It keeps you logged in for up to 180 days, or until you log out. The arcade keeps only a scrambled copy of it.
arcade.privacy.what_stays_each_machine_s: What remains: each machine's record (using only a random account number), money records for machines in arcades you've hosted, and Cloudflare's logs and backups until they're deleted (see above). Your device may keep your passkey; you can remove it in your device's passkey settings.
arcade.privacy.what_the_arcade_does_not: What the arcade does not do
arcade.privacy.what_the_arcade_keeps_abo: What the arcade keeps about you, why, and for how long.
arcade.privacy.you_can_look_round_the: You can explore the arcade without an account. Your games stay on your device; the arcade never uploads your game files.
arcade.privacy.your_browser_keeps_your_g: Your browser stores your games, the arcade you're building and your sound settings on this device. Clearing this site's data in your browser will remove them.
arcade.privacy.your_passkey_s_public_hal: The public part of your passkey, its ID and the date it was last used. The arcade uses these to check it's you. The private part never leaves your device, and the arcade never asks for an email address or password.
arcade.privacy.your_picture_if_you_add: Your picture, if you add one. Anyone using the arcade can see it.
arcade.privacy.your_player_name_other_pl: Your player name, which other players can see when you're playing a machine, for example. It doesn't have to be your real name.
arcade.privacy.your_wallet_your_balance_: Your wallet balance and each payment into or out of a machine, including the machine and time. This is play money only; you can't buy it or cash it in.
